newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya to sell off interest in tourism companies.
newsitem.headline: Kenya to sell off interest in tourism companies.

text.p: Kenya's parastatal reform committee (PRPC) on Tuesday announced that it had approved the sale of government shares in the tourism body Kenya Tourism Development Corporation (KTDC).
A statement by the Investment Coordinator of PRPC, George Mitine, said the divestiture was part of an ongoing privatisation programme in Kenya.
Out of five companies, only the five star Serena Lodges & Hotels would be sold through a public share offer. The rest would be divested through a pre-emptive rights issue to existing share holders.

Some 12,893,000 shares of KTDC in Safari Lodges and Properties, the company that runs the Serena chain of Hotels, would be floated at the Nairobi Stock Exchange. Details of the flotation including the share price would be released at a later date.
A further 3,816,328 shares of Serena in Tourism Promotion Services would be sold through a rights issue.

The privatisation comes in the wake of a delay by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) of $37 million disbursment under a soft-loans programme over what the fund saw as slow progress in the privatisation process.
The IMF in Nairobi said the outstanding issues were structural and revolved around privatisation because donors did not want the Kenyan government to continue bailing out ailing parastatals.

Government interest in Sunset Hotel -- 95.4 percent would be sold at 105 million to Piedmont Investment Limited, while 34.1 percent in Kenya National Properties would be sold at an offer price of 227 per share.

Also approved were 57,870 shares (45 percent) in Polysynthetic E.A to Hoechst E.A through a preemptive rights issue at 869 and 63,334 shares (40 percent) in Dawa Pharmaceuticals at an offer price of 73.
